record.narrative: No prior claims exist, so the first screen focuses on predictors with adequate cell sizes and dependency outcomes that are either highly variable or clinically interesting as negative-score outcomes. Binary predictors such as feature_034, feature_002, feature_060, feature_021, and feature_027 provide balanced exposure groups, while feature_001 tests a rarer marker with still adequate exposed count. The negative-direction hypotheses state that the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency; positive-direction hypotheses state that the exposed group has a higher, less negative score, implying weaker dependency. Interaction hypotheses test whether a second marker modifies the exposure-outcome relationship in the same eligible population. All hypotheses are initially unresolved because magnitude and uncertainty must be evaluated against Welch intervals and the 10% relative difference criterion, with additional attention to absolute dependency-score differences because some outcome means are close to zero.

All twelve newly registered comparisons are currently untested and fit within the 12-analysis limit. Running the full initial screen evaluates balanced binary predictors across high-variance dependency outcomes, includes one rare exposure, and tests two interaction hypotheses in parallel. These results will reveal whether effect sizes and Welch intervals meet the 10% relative-difference threshold and guide focused subgroup and outcome follow-up in later iterations.

The first screen produced mostly imprecise null results. H1, H2, H8, and H9 have point estimates near zero and do not support the registered directions. H3 shows a point estimate opposite the claimed direction, and H12 has a point estimate above the 10% clinical threshold, but both 95% intervals include zero, so neither supports a decisive conclusion. H4, H5, H7, H8, H9, and H11 are also uninformative for their claimed directions. H10 supports its direction with estimate +0.0155 for outcome_005, but the interval includes zero and spans below the clinical threshold; it remains unresolved but active as follow-up predictor/outcome testing may clarify. The only interval excluding zero is R6/H6: outcome_013 with feature_027, direction -1. Because the signed estimate is negative (-0.0270, 95% CI -0.0502 to -0.0037), this is evidence against the pre-specified negative direction rather than evidence supporting it; raw-exposed minus comparator appears positive, implying less negative outcome_013 scores, i.e. weaker dependency. Its absolute magnitude is about 10% of the outcome_013 mean, but the relative interval likely spans from small to clinically meaningful, and it is one significant result among 12 tests. Therefore H6 is not accepted as originally stated; it is kept active with independent validation requested. I also registered a reversal/refinement with direction +1 for the same comparison and additional tests of feature_027 across outcomes to see whether the opposite direction is consistent rather than idiosyncratic. The other new claims broadly cover remaining outcomes using balanced binary predictors, with no prior accepted claim being forced.

The independent validation for H6 does not support the original hypothesis and substantially weakens the only borderline discovery signal from the first screen. H6 tested whether feature_027=1 has a more negative outcome_013 score than feature_027=0, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency. The discovery result R6 had signed estimate -0.0270, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast was positive: outcome_013 was less negative in the exposed group, opposite to the registered negative direction. The validation result R13 was signed estimate -0.00078, again a tiny positive raw contrast, with a very wide independent interval that includes zero and spans both sides of the clinical threshold. Because the point estimate and discovery interval refuted the registered negative direction and the independent check did not rescue it, I reject H6. The reversal H13, testing the opposite positive raw contrast, is not accepted either: R6 is statistically distinguishable from zero but only borderline against the 10% relative-difference threshold, while the independent validation is near zero and imprecise. I close the exact feature_027-outcome_013 claim rather than continue pursuing it, since the independent validation did not confirm it.

Several first-round claims can now be resolved more definitively as negative for their claimed clinically meaningful direction. H2, H4, H5, H8, and H9 have intervals whose maximum support for the claimed direction is below the approximate 10% clinical threshold, so I reject those claimed directional meaningful differences and close them. H3 also rejects its original positive raw contrast for outcome_006; however, its raw point estimate is negative, about 12% stronger dependency, and its interval does not exclude a clinically meaningful negative raw contrast. Therefore, rather than treating H3 as a final null, I registered H25 as a post-hoc reversal of H3 to test whether feature_027=1 is associated with stronger outcome_006 dependency. This remains only a hypothesis for follow-up because it was motivated by the discovery evidence.

At this stage, no predictor-outcome pair is accepted as scientifically meaningful in this dataset. The most useful next analysis is to run the already registered broad screen H14-H24 plus the H3 reversal H25. This will cover the remaining outcomes using the balanced binary predictors already selected and test whether feature_002 has a more consistent association with outcome_006. Claims remain associations within the supplied dataset only; none support causality or generalizability.

The next round should move beyond the failed feature_027 lead and focus on predictors with adequate cell sizes in high-variance dependency outcomes. The main claims with direction -1 test whether the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, meaning stronger CRISPR dependency; the plausible alternative is that the exposure is unrelated or associated with a less negative score. Feature_060 is prioritized for outcome_001 and outcome_006 because the H12 interaction signal on outcome_001 was directionally relevant but underpowered, and outcome_006 has high variance and a low absolute 10% threshold. Feature_002 is followed up across outcome_001 and outcome_011 because the H3 raw pattern suggested stronger dependency in the exposed group. Feature_012, feature_050, and feature_045 provide new binary markers with approximately 375-510 exposed cells, allowing reasonably stable Welch comparisons on outcome_005, outcome_006, outcome_008, outcome_011, and outcome_014. The two interaction hypotheses test whether feature_002 modifies the feature_060 association, using the same eligible population and comparing the contrast in feature_002=1 versus feature_002=0. All are framed as dataset associations rather than causal claims, and any apparent effect will still be judged against interval width, the 10% relative-difference threshold, and the caution that near-zero means make relative thresholds volatile.

I selected 12 untested main-effect comparisons that both complete coverage of outcome_012, outcome_003, outcome_007, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_002, and outcome_016 and follow up the most informative Round-1 predictors: feature_060 and feature_002. H26 and H27 test whether feature_060 is associated with stronger dependency for outcome_001 and outcome_006; H29 and H30 test feature_002 on outcome_001 and outcome_011 because the original feature_002 contrast in outcome_006 was in the stronger-dependency direction although its original claimed direction was rejected. The remaining H17-H24 analyses give balanced binary-predictor screens across the still-untested outcomes using feature_034, feature_002, feature_060, and feature_065. I deliberately deferred the feature_012, feature_050, feature_045, and interaction claims for now because there is no accepted lead yet and interpreting interactions is more useful after the corresponding main effects are estimated. All comparisons are treated as within-dataset associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

The new screen was mostly negative for the registered stronger-dependency directions. For most claims, the signed point estimate was small and the upper 95% bound remained below the approximate 10% relative threshold, so I reject those claims as evidence of a clinically meaningful difference in the hypothesized direction within this dataset. Specifically, H17-H24, H29, and H30 have maximum support for the claimed signed effect below about 10% of the absolute outcome mean; several of them even point in the opposite raw direction. I am not accepting those opposite-direction findings because they were not pre-specified and remain only exploratory possibilities.

H27 is the only new result with a point estimate above the 10% threshold. Its signed estimate for outcome_006 with feature_060 is +0.0194, about 11% of the absolute outcome mean and indicating a more negative score in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency. However, its interval is wide and includes both zero and clinically meaningful values in the opposite direction, so the current evidence is not decisive. Because outcome_006 has a near-zero mean and high variance, the absolute 10% threshold is relatively small and susceptible to inflation or spurious borderline findings. H27 is nevertheless the most plausible follow-up candidate: it is a main effect with a pre-registered direction and a point estimate beyond the clinical threshold, so I request independent validation of H27. H26 remains unresolved but deferred: outcome_001 has a larger absolute mean and thus a higher threshold, the point estimate is only about 4%, and although the interval upper bound crosses 10%, it is much weaker than H27. The other new claims do not justify validation because their intervals do not plausibly support the registered clinically meaningful direction.

H27 tested whether feature_060=1 is associated with a more negative outcome_006 dependency score than feature_060=0, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency, in the full eligible population. The signed discovery estimate R15 was +0.0194, which is only modestly above the approximate 10% threshold for outcome_006: the absolute outcome_006 mean is about 0.175, so the relevant 10% scale is about 0.0175. The discovery interval was wide and not decisive, -0.0153 to +0.0541, including both no effect and clinically meaningful effects in either direction. The independent validation R26 was much weaker: signed estimate +0.0020, only about 1% of the absolute outcome_006 mean, with an independent interval -0.0489 to +0.0529. That interval is extremely wide because validation intervals account for the maximum validation count, so it does not formally rule out a large effect, and it overlaps the discovery estimate. However, the validation point estimate is far below the clinical threshold and does not corroborate the discovery signal. Taken together, the evidence does not support accepting a scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency association between feature_060 and outcome_006 in the full population. I therefore leave H27 unresolved rather than accept it, but I close the exact full-population feature_060-outcome_006 claim because the independent check has failed to support it and further exact analysis is unlikely to be more informative than focused effect-modification or alternative predictor screening.

More broadly, the current evidence supports no accepted predictor-outcome pair as a clinically meaningful association in this dataset. The feature_027-outcome_013 route from the first round failed validation and is closed. H27 was the only second-round full-population candidate with a discovery point estimate near the 10% threshold, and validation reduced it to a near-null estimate. Most other Round-2 main effects were not promising for the registered clinically meaningful direction: H17-H24, H29, and H30 were rejected because their intervals did not plausibly support the claimed direction, and several point estimates were opposite the hypothesized raw direction. These are not accepted opposite-direction findings; they are primarily evidence against the registered claims.

The most informative remaining leads are unresolved but not validated borderline signals. H25 tests feature_002=1 versus feature_002=0 for outcome_006 in the stronger-dependency direction and has a signed discovery estimate of +0.0209, about 12% of the absolute outcome_006 mean, with a wide interval that still crosses the 10% threshold. H10 tests feature_065=1 versus 0 for outcome_005 and has a signed discovery estimate of +0.0155, about 6% of the absolute outcome_005 mean, with an interval that reaches beyond the 10% threshold but remains imprecise. H26 for outcome_001 is also imprecise and currently lower priority because its point estimate is only about 4%. The next useful step is to analyze the already registered feature_012, feature_050, feature_045, and feature_002-modified feature_060 claims, especially H36 and H37, which test whether feature_002 modifies feature_060 associations. If those screens do not produce a stronger signal, the next validation should likely target H25 or H10 rather than exact H27. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations; none support causality or external generalization.

After two broad main-effect screens, no predictor-outcome pair has been accepted as clinically meaningful. The most informative remaining signals are focused: H12 suggests that feature_060 may be associated with stronger outcome_001 dependency specifically when feature_021=1, H25 suggests a possible stronger-dependency effect of feature_002 for outcome_006, and H10 suggests a possible feature_065-outcome_005 association. These should be tested as context-specific hypotheses rather than pursued as failed full-population main effects. I therefore propose three subgroup refinements: within feature_021=1, does feature_060=1 show stronger outcome_001 dependency; within feature_060=1, does feature_002=1 show stronger outcome_006 dependency; and within feature_002=1, does feature_065=1 show stronger outcome_005 dependency. These are plausible alternative explanations for imprecise full-population estimates: the signal may be localized, diluted, or absent depending on effect modification. I also add a new broad binary-marker screen, feature_012 for outcome_001, because feature_012 already has registered tests for other outcomes and outcome_001 has a larger threshold, making any accepted effect more robust. The alternative hypotheses are that these exposures are unrelated to the outcome in the named subgroup, or that they are associated with weaker dependency. All comparisons remain associations within the supplied dataset and do not imply causality or external generalizability. I close the low-priority feature_027 reversal claims H14-H16 to prioritize focused and high-value untested analyses.

I selected the 12 currently untested active claims to maximize new information while avoiding reruns that would reuse the same discovery sample. These analyses test: (1) feature_050 for outcome_006 (H28); (2) feature_012 across outcome_001, outcome_005, outcome_006, outcome_008, and outcome_011 (H41, H33, H34, H32, H31); (3) feature_045 for outcome_014 (H35); (4) whether feature_002 modifies feature_060 associations for outcome_006 and outcome_001 (H36 and H37); and (5) focused subgroup refinements of prior borderline signals: feature_060 within feature_021=1 for outcome_001 (H38), feature_002 within feature_060=1 for outcome_006 (H39), and feature_065 within feature_002=1 for outcome_005 (H40). These are all within-dataset association tests. At appraisal I will compare signed estimates with each outcome's 10% relative-scale threshold and judge interval precision before deciding whether any claim merits validation or rejection.

The new screen did not produce a claim I can accept. Several claims have registered-direction estimates either opposite to the claim or with upper bounds below the approximate 10% relative threshold; I reject those because they do not support the hypothesized clinically meaningful difference, while noting that I am not accepting any unpre-specified opposite-direction findings. For H31-H33, feature_012 shows either negative signed estimates or interval upper bounds below the relevant threshold for outcome_011, outcome_008, and outcome_005. H35 is registered as stronger dependency for feature_045 on outcome_014, but the signed estimate is negative and large, pointing opposite to the claim; I reject it rather than promote an unplanned opposite-direction result.

Most other new results are unresolved but not promising enough for continued full-population discovery. H28, H34, H36, H40, and H41 have wide intervals that sometimes touch the 10% scale, but their point estimates are far from clinically meaningful and their intervals are centered near null. For outcome_006, the absolute 10% threshold is especially volatile because the outcome mean is near zero; I treat borderline positive estimates on outcome_006 more skeptically than those on outcome_001 or outcome_005.

The most informative new candidate is H38: feature_060=1 versus feature_060=0 among feature_021=1 for outcome_001. The signed estimate is +0.0529, above the outcome_001 10% threshold of about 0.0415, suggesting stronger dependency in the exposed group within this subgroup. However, the cells are small (195 and 211) and the interval is wide (-0.0191 to +0.1249), so the discovery evidence alone is not enough. Because H38 is a direct main-effect subgroup hypothesis motivated by the earlier H12 interaction signal, independent validation is worthwhile despite multiplicity. I request validation of H38. If validation corroborates a meaningful stronger-dependency association, the claim can be assessed as subgroup-specific and within-dataset only. If validation is null or opposite, the feature_060/feature_021 subgroup route should be closed.

H37 is also at the outcome_001 threshold but is an interaction with a very wide interval; it is less direct than H38 and remains deferred. I registered a refinement H42 to test feature_060 within feature_002=1 directly if H37 needs interpretation. H39 shows a larger relative point on outcome_006 than the full-population H25, but outcome_006's near-zero mean, high variance, and the earlier failed validation of feature_060-outcome_006 make it lower priority for the one voluntary validation request in this iteration. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

Supported findings: none. The accepted set remains empty; no predictor-outcome comparison has evidence that I can accept as a scientifically meaningful difference at the 10% relative-outcome scale within this dataset.

Due assessments: H6 is the feature_027-outcome_013 stronger-dependency claim. The discovery R6 was already opposite the registered direction (signed estimate -0.0270, interval entirely on the opposite side of zero), and the independent validation R13 is near null (signed estimate -0.0008, interval -0.0399 to +0.0383). I keep H6 rejected and closed. H3 is the feature_002-outcome_006 claim in the opposite raw direction from the later stronger-dependency claim H25. The new validation R40 is signed -0.0150 (interval -0.0646 to +0.0345), so it does not support the weaker-dependency direction claimed by H3. I keep H3 rejected. The same raw evidence is more favorable to the reverse H25 stronger-dependency claim, but not strong enough to accept.

H38 is the most informative new result. It tested feature_060=1 versus 0 within feature_021=1 for outcome_001 in the stronger-dependency direction. The discovery R35 estimate is +0.0529, above the approximate 10% scale for outcome_001 (about 0.0415), but the cells are small and the interval is wide. The independent validation R39 is a nonreplication: signed estimate -0.0060, far below the threshold, with a very wide interval -0.1092 to +0.0973. I do not accept H38. I keep it formally unresolved rather than fully reject it because the independent interval is too wide to exclude clinically meaningful positive effects, but the exact feature_021=1 subgroup route is closed as not worth further pursuit.

Negative or unsupported routes so far include: feature_027-outcome_013 (H6 and the reverse H13 after validation), exact feature_060-outcome_006 full-population (H27, failed validation), most feature_012 screens, feature_045-outcome_014 in the registered direction, and the feature_060/feature_021 outcome_001 subgroup route just tested. These rejections mean the registered clinically meaningful claims are not supported; they do not prove the absence of all effects, especially where independent intervals are wide.

Most informative remaining leads: H25 (full-population feature_002 for outcome_006 in the stronger-dependency direction) remains unresolved but active. Its discovery R3 is +0.0209, above the approximate outcome_006 10% scale of 0.0175, and its validation R40 is +0.0150, just below threshold, with a wide interval -0.0345 to +0.0646. The direction is consistent across discovery and validation, but the evidence is not decisive. H39, the feature_002 effect within feature_060=1 for outcome_006, has a larger discovery point (+0.0256) and is now kept active as a subgroup refinement. H42 remains the best next untested analysis: feature_060 within feature_002=1 for outcome_001, which directly interprets the threshold-level but imprecise interaction H37. H10 and H40 for feature_065-outcome_005 remain weak because their point estimates are below the approximate 0.025 threshold, despite intervals that reach the threshold.

Next plan: analyze H42 first. If H42 yields a threshold-level estimate with a reasonably informative interval, validate it. If H42 is null or imprecise and no better full-population signal appears, prioritize independent validation of H39 over repeated exact H25. Avoid further feature_027 and exact H27 analyses. All statements remain within-dataset associations; they do not establish causality or external generalizability.

No predictor-outcome association has yet been accepted at the approximate 10% relative outcome scale. The strongest current lead remains the outcome_006 feature_002 route, where the discovery and validation estimates are directionally consistent but not decisive, and the still-untested H42 is the direct outcome_001 feature_060 effect within feature_002=1. I therefore propose comparisons that decompose the main existing leads and also test two prior opposite-direction signals formally.

First, H35 was registered as feature_045=1 versus 0 for stronger outcome_014 dependency, but the signed estimate was opposite to that claim. The raw pattern was positive, and outcome_014 has a small absolute 10% threshold of about 0.0093. I propose a reversed claim for feature_045 on outcome_014: feature_045=1 is associated with weaker dependency, i.e. a higher outcome_014 score, than feature_045=0. This is a new claim rather than an acceptance of the old claim because the original registered hypothesis was not supported. The alternative hypotheses are null or the original stronger-dependency direction. Similarly, H11 was an interaction for feature_034 by feature_002=1 on outcome_014 in the stronger-dependency direction but produced an opposite-signed estimate; I propose the reversed interaction to test whether feature_002 status modifies feature_034 association in the opposite direction.

Second, I register direct subgroup refinements of the outcome_001 feature_060 and outcome_006 feature_002/feature_060 leads. For outcome_001, H42 directly tests feature_060 within feature_002=1; the new proposal tests the complement, feature_060 within feature_002=0. This will clarify whether H42's expected threshold-level signal is localized to feature_002=1 or diffuse across feature_002 strata. For outcome_006, I register feature_002 within feature_060=0 to complement H39, and feature_060 within feature_002=1 as the direct effect behind the H36 interaction. These are more interpretable than relying only on interaction contrasts, especially because the prior interaction intervals are wide.

Third, I add limited broad screens: outcome_006 with untested binary predictors feature_020 and feature_052, plus binary categorical feature_054 level_001 versus level_002, and outcome_001 with feature_065. Outcome_006 is prioritized because it currently has the most active borderline signal and its approximate absolute 10% threshold is about 0.0175, although its mean is near zero and high variance make interpretation less stable. Outcome_001 is included for feature_065 because feature_065 has prior borderline evidence for outcome_005 and a related outcome_001 test has not been performed; the approximate outcome_001 threshold is larger, about 0.0415. The feature_054 exposure is nominal, not ordered, and the alternative hypotheses are no association or the opposite direction. All proposals are within-dataset association tests and do not imply causality or external generalizability.

I selected the currently untested active claims that add new discovery information and follow the most promising leads. H42 is the highest-priority direct subgroup test of feature_060 within feature_002=1 for outcome_001, and H45 gives the complementary feature_002=0 analysis to determine whether any effect is localized or diffuse. H46 and H47 decompose the feature_002/feature_060 relationship for outcome_006, complementing the active full-population and subgroup leads H25/H39/H36. H48-H50 are limited broad screens for outcome_006, and H51 is a single related outcome_001 screen for feature_065. I did not select H43 or H44 because their displayed evidence is already inherited from the parent discovery results and rerunning them would not add a new sample. I also omitted closed feature_027 routes and previously tested claims to allocate analysis effort to new evidence.

No new result can be accepted at the approximate 10% absolute-outcome scale. The most informative result is H42: feature_060=1 versus 0 among feature_002=1 for outcome_001 has a signed estimate of +0.0362, below the outcome_001 threshold of about 0.0415, with a wide interval (-0.0096 to +0.0821). The complement H45 is null and has an upper bound below the threshold (+0.0397; threshold 0.0415), so I reject H45. Together these results suggest that any outcome_001 feature_060 signal, if present, is confined to feature_002=1 and is not diffuse; however H42 is still threshold-adjacent rather than threshold-level and is less compelling than the outcome_006 H39 lead.

For outcome_006 (threshold about 0.0175), H46 and H47 decompose the feature_002/feature_060 leads. H46 has a below-threshold point estimate (+0.0158) and a wide interval, so it is not a good independent target and is closed. H47 has a threshold-level point estimate (+0.0241), but the full-population feature_060-outcome_006 route already failed independent validation (H27), making H47 a high-risk post hoc subgroup route. H39 remains the better validation candidate because it tests the feature_002 effect within feature_060=1 (+0.0256, interval reaching well above threshold), and the full-population feature_002-outcome_006 evidence has shown directionally consistent but imprecise discovery/validation estimates. I therefore request independent validation of H39.

H48 is rejected for the registered stronger-dependency direction: the signed estimate is opposite the claim and its positive-side upper bound is only +0.0079, far below the 0.0175 threshold. The raw opposite signal is threshold-level, but it is an unpre-specified post hoc inversion in a high-variance outcome and should not be accepted as a clinically meaningful finding without a prior registered reversed claim and further independent evidence. The remaining broad screens H49-H51 are centered near null, with point estimates far below their thresholds; I close them as unresolved rather than formally reject because their wide intervals do not entirely exclude threshold-level effects. All conclusions remain within-dataset associations.

Supported findings: none. After the newly delivered independent validation of H39 and the response deadline for H27, the accepted claim set remains empty; no predictor-outcome comparison has evidence that I can accept as a scientifically meaningful difference at the approximate 10 percent relative-outcome scale within this dataset. Due assessment H27 is the exact full-population feature_060 claim for outcome_006 in the stronger-dependency direction. Its discovery evidence was threshold-level in the signed direction, plus 0.0194 with interval -0.0153 to +0.0541, but the independent validation is essentially null, plus 0.0020 with interval -0.0489 to +0.0529. The validation does not corroborate a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association, so I reject H27 and close the exact feature_060-outcome_006 route. This is a negative finding for the registered claim, not proof that no such effect exists, because outcome_006 is noisy and the validation interval still includes positive values above the approximate threshold of 0.0175. Due assessment H39 is the feature_002 effect within feature_060=1 for outcome_006 in the stronger-dependency direction. The discovery estimate is threshold-level in the claimed direction, plus 0.0256 with interval -0.0232 to +0.0744, but the independent validation is opposite the claim, signed minus 0.0226 with wide interval -0.0957 to +0.0505. The discovery and validation are inconsistent, and the independent interval is too wide to support either a clean positive effect or a clean opposite effect. Because this was the best remaining outcome_006 subgroup candidate and it failed independent validation, I reject H39 as the registered hypothesis and close it. I also close the broader outcome_006 feature_002 and feature_060 decomposition: H25 remains unresolved but closed because full-population feature_002 was directionally consistent across discovery and validation but below threshold on validation, signed plus 0.0150 with interval -0.0345 to +0.0646; H47 remains unresolved but closed because its direct feature_060 effect within feature_002=1 was threshold-level at plus 0.0241 but is tied to the failed exact feature_060 route and failed H39 subgroup evidence. Negative or unsupported routes now include feature_027-outcome_013 in both registered directions after validation, exact feature_060-outcome_006, the feature_002 and feature_060 outcome_006 decomposition, most feature_012 screens, the registered feature_045 stronger-dependency claim on outcome_014, H45 as the feature_002=0 complement for outcome_001 feature_060, H48 in its registered direction, and the feature_060-feature_021 outcome_001 subgroup route after failed validation. The most promising unresolved leads are not yet accepted but are more informative than the closed outcome_006 routes: H43, the reversed full-population feature_045 claim on outcome_014, has a threshold-level signed estimate of plus 0.0218 for weaker dependency, far above the small outcome_014 threshold of about 0.0093, although the interval is wide, -0.0153 to +0.0590. H44, the reversed feature_034 by feature_002 interaction for outcome_014, is also threshold-level, plus 0.0377, but very imprecise, -0.0262 to +0.1016. The new proposals formalize the raw opposite feature_020 signal for outcome_006 and decompose the H44 interaction into direct feature_034 effects within the feature_002 strata; they also test whether the reversed feature_045 signal on outcome_014 has coherence on larger-threshold outcomes outcome_001 and outcome_011. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of the strongest existing reversed outcome_014 lead, preferably H43 because it is a main effect and is more interpretable than the H44 interaction. If H43 fails validation, the next best candidates are H44 and the proposed reversed feature_020-outcome_006 claim, followed by the outcome_001 feature_060 within feature_002=1 route through H42 and H37, where H42 is just below threshold at plus 0.0362 versus threshold about 0.0415 and H37 is interaction-level but imprecise. All conclusions remain associations within this supplied dataset and do not imply causality or external generalizability.

The accepted claim set remains empty, but two reversed main-effect leads are now the most scientifically useful targets for refinement and eventual validation: H43, where feature_045=1 versus 0 is associated with a higher outcome_014 score, i.e. weaker dependency, with signed estimate +0.0218 compared with an approximate 10% scale of 0.0093; and H52, where feature_020=1 versus 0 is associated with a higher outcome_006 score, signed estimate +0.0407 compared with an approximate 10% scale of 0.0175. Both discovery intervals are wide, so the next best use of analysis is to test whether these are broad, biologically coherent associations or fragile subgroup artifacts. I also keep the earlier outcome_001 feature_060 within feature_002=1 lead in reserve, but it is less mature than H43 and H52 because the direct estimate is slightly below threshold and the exact feature_060 outcome_006 route already failed validation. I propose three groups of comparisons. First, decompose the reversed feature_045-outcome_014 association by feature_002 and by feature_034. The hypothesis is that feature_045=1 is associated with a higher outcome_014 score, i.e. weaker dependency, within each stratum; alternatives are null or an opposite lower-score association. This distinguishes a broad main effect from an effect driven by correlation with feature_002 or feature_034, and it clarifies whether the existing H44 interaction evidence reflects a broader outcome_014 biology or a narrower feature_034-by-feature_002 effect. Second, decompose the reversed feature_020-outcome_006 association by feature_002. The hypothesis is that feature_020=1 is associated with a higher outcome_006 score within both feature_002 strata; alternatives are null or opposite. Because outcome_006 is noisy and the exact feature_060/feature_002 outcome_006 routes have failed, a localized or inconsistent feature_020 signal should not be overinterpreted, while a consistent positive decomposition would support independent validation. Third, add limited coherence screens. If feature_045 or feature_020 marks a broader dependency phenotype, positive higher-score shifts should appear in related outcomes; the alternatives are null or opposite shifts. These include feature_020 on outcome_014, outcome_001, and outcome_011, and feature_045 on outcome_008 and outcome_013. I expect feature_045 to be most credible if the signal is coherent across outcomes with the smaller threshold or across nearby outcomes, while feature_020 is worth testing because H52 is threshold-level on point estimate despite being imprecise. All proposals are within-dataset association hypotheses and do not claim causality or external generalizability. The next appraise should prioritize independent validation of H43 first because it is a main effect with a threshold-level point estimate and a small outcome_014 scale; if H43 validation fails, H52 or a consistent H52 decomposition would be the next validation candidate, while inconsistent decompositions should be used to close these routes.

I selected 12 untested active claims that add new discovery evidence and directly refine the two strongest reversed leads, H43 and H52, without rerunning comparisons that already have evidence. H57-H60 decompose the reversed outcome_014 feature_045 main effect by feature_002 and feature_034. This asks whether the signed plus 0.0218 outcome_014 signal is a broad higher-score, weaker-dependency association or is driven by correlated feature_002 or feature_034 strata. H53-H54 decompose the feature_034-by-feature_002 interaction lead H44 into the stratum-level effects that generate it. H55-H56 test coherence of the feature_045 reversed signal on outcome_001 and outcome_011, where larger outcome scales make acceptance more demanding but positive associations would support a broader predictor-outcome pattern rather than an isolated outcome_014 result.
